propositions: git fetch to GitHub mirror intermittently hangs past 300s wall-clock timeout due to absence of throughput-keyed abort (http.lowSpeedLimit / http.lowSpeedTime config)
a byte-starved connection that accepts but sends zero bytes is bounded only by the 300s subprocess timeout, not by transfer rate
passing -c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=10 to git causes stalled fetches to abort in ~10s with 'Operation too slow' error
legitimately slow but progressing transfers (e.g. 90s full clone at 1 MB/s) are not aborted by throughput-keyed limits, only truly stalled connections
in-process retry of low-speed abort failures (bounded attempts) reduces stall impact from 300s per review to ~30s total while preserving non-retry behavior for auth and ref failures
